title: TransArmor Processing Considerations
source: Appendix AA-1 through AA-6; Elements 12 and 102; Appendix I-53/I-54 Table 052
applicability: Bounded TransArmor logical-field profiles: RSA/PKI, TA-VE Cipher Hidden Encryption, TDES/DUKPT, Ingenico OnGuard FPE, AES DUKPT, and Token Only. Not cryptographic or full wire certification.
sourceNotes: Initialization calls for Key Load to obtain Key/Key ID and RegiStart to register the device; full protocols are in the external ATL105 Specifications Update for TransArmor Processing.
Element 2 TAP header is TAP(3)+sequence(6)+EDATA identifier(1)+Key ID(11)+Token Type ID(4); Token Type is a First Data-assigned alphanumeric value for Single use or MultiPay.
Identifiers 1/2/3 represent initial encrypted Track1/Track2/manual PAN for PKI, TDES/DUKPT, OnGuard and AES DUKPT. Identifier 4 is initial Token Only with unencrypted Track1/Track2/manual PAN.
PKI uses the loaded Key ID. TDES/OnGuard/AES use 11 zero header bytes; related Key ID data is supplied through Additional TransArmor Data as applicable.
TA-VE identifiers 6/7/M identify PIN pads through BUYPASS terminal number, Element 79 pump/lane number, or Segment 111 Table 018 Card Acceptor Terminal ID respectively.
TA-VE Key ID is 5-byte Merchant Domain, semicolon, 5-byte Merchant Brand; EDATA begins a boarded alphanumeric processor code of up to 16 characters followed by colon and encrypted data.
Encrypted manual PAN is followed by actual FS and unencrypted MMYY, including manually keyed TA-VE.

Identifier 0 is subsequent token use. The identifier table says zero-filled subsequent Key ID with/without semicolon; AA-4/AA-5 examples retain original nonzero Key IDs. This conflict remains REVIEW_REQUIRED.
Initial response Account Number supplies the token used subsequently, including completion and cancellation examples. Expiration is stored and sent unencrypted in subsequent Element 12.
Initial PKI Account Number is prefixed with 00 plus the first six Merchant Number bytes before encryption. Element 102 locates Merchant Number after the first four device/state characters.
Failed Token Only retrieval returns Decline Code 4M in Element 26. Successful retrieval alone does not establish authorization approval.

Element 30 value 8 signals expiring/expired Key ID and the need to update Key and Key ID. Element 48 K is Key Load; Element 83 K is approved and L rejected (merchant not enabled or invalid/outdated signing key). PKI load Element 102 Device Type is ++.

Table 052 allows Additional TransArmor Data for longer Key ID/special device type. Appendix I describes maximum 100 bytes, sub-table 01 KSN up to 40 required for TDES/OnGuard/AES, sub-table 02 Device Type up to 8 required for AES and optional for TDES/OnGuard. Exact TLV ordering/long-Key-ID representation is not invented.

AA-4 shows a PKI authorization/response/completion/response; AA-5/AA-6 show a TA-VE authorization/response/cancellation/response. Encrypted blocks are illustrative and need not decrypt; periods denote field separators in examples.

Examples are not real cryptographic fixtures and do not settle the contradictory subsequent Key ID rule. Assignment, device registration, key provenance, token association and storage require external evidence.

businessRequirements.title: TAP widths, sequence equality, known identifier, Token Type representation and encrypted EDATA maximum 400 bytes.
All eight EDATA identifiers, encryption-method Key ID rules, TA-VE processor prefix and device routing, manual FS/MMYY, subsequent Key ID conflict.
Reuse initial response token and stored unencrypted expiration for subsequent token transactions.
Token Only retrieval failure returns 4M, without inferring approval from successful retrieval.
Load Type K, response K/L by supplied outcome, PKI load Device Type ++; rejection causes remain externally evidenced.
Download Indicator 8 requires Key/Key ID refresh; actual terminal behavior is external.
Initial PKI pre-encryption prefix is 00 plus first six Merchant Number bytes; only controlled synthetic evidence is used.
Table 052 known KSN/device requirements and widths; longer Key ID and exact wire TLV remain reviewed.
Initialization calls for Key Load and RegiStart; external update document is needed for protocol certification.
Synthetic ciphertext and matching token/identity strings do not prove cryptographic validity, boarding assignments, actual token association, or durable storage.

fixtureSemantics: Shallow merge payload over fixtureDefaults; maps replace defaults. Every fixture targets one assessment and is synthetic, not a network-authenticated transaction.
